P30-I12-W02.outcome: live per-lane pgid registry on FleetRun; fleet.drive wired live in server.py

success_criteria.measurable_signal: test_lane_registers_pgid asserts lane.pgid==spawned pgid keyed by (wave_id,attempt); test_lane_deregisters_on_close drops the entry
success_criteria.text: Dispatching a lane records lane.pgid as the spawned child's real process-group id keyed by (wave_id, attempt); closing or killing the lane deregisters it so the registry holds exactly the in-flight lanes.

success_criteria.measurable_signal: test_lane_no_pid_is_unkillable asserts lane.pgid is None and a kill of it returns the typed not-found
success_criteria.text: A spawn that returns no pid leaves lane.pgid None and marks the lane unkillable rather than recording a fabricated pid; the registry never holds a pid the OS does not own.

P30-I12-W02.title: DL-2 live per-lane pid registry on FleetRun for kill and reattach

P30-I12-W03.description: Replace the agent.kill placeholder (returns killed=false today, keyed on wave_id+attempt) with a real signal: resolve the FleetRun lane from (wave_id, attempt) via the W02 registry, then signal lane.pgid - H/halt SIGTERM (graceful), K/kill SIGKILL (hard). The TUI K/H keys go live; the lane transitions to a killed terminal.
P30-I12-W03.outcome: Real agent.kill resolves lane registry then signals pgid (SIGKILL/SIGTERM)

success_criteria.measurable_signal: test_agent_kill_resolves_lane_from_registry asserts the (wave_id,attempt)->lane lookup then os.killpg on lane.pgid; result killed True; lane killed
success_criteria.text: agent.kill(wave_id, attempt) resolves the target lane via the FleetRun registry and signals lane.pgid with SIGKILL (signal=kill) or SIGTERM (signal=halt), returns killed=true, and transitions the lane to a killed terminal that deregisters; the lookup is named, not just the os.killpg call.

success_criteria.measurable_signal: test_agent_kill_unknown_lane_not_found returns killed False with reason; test_agent_kill_already_dead returns killed True without raising
success_criteria.text: agent.kill for a wave with no live lane returns a typed not-found (killed=false with a reason), never a faked kill; a ProcessLookupError on the pgid degrades to killed=true already-dead, not a crash.

P30-I12-W03.title: DL-3 real agent.kill resolves the lane registry then signals pgid

P30-I12-W04.description: Give the loop budget teeth: at the EU/$/wave cap stop claiming new waves. Graceful-drain (default) lets in-flight lanes finish then ends terminal_reason=budget; the arm-modal hard-halt toggle instead kills in-flight lanes at the cap. Reads the EUCAP runtime delta for the live EU/$ figures (off the hard-coded 0.0).
P30-I12-W04.outcome: Budget HALT teeth: graceful-drain (terminal_reason=budget) + hard-halt kill toggle

success_criteria.measurable_signal: test_budget_cap_blocks_next_claim asserts zero new claims past the cap; test_graceful_drain_finishes_inflight ends DONE terminal_reason=budget
success_criteria.text: When cumulative spend reaches euCap (or usdCap/wavesCap), the loop claims no further waves; under graceful drain the in-flight lanes finish and the run ends DONE with terminal_reason=budget.

success_criteria.measurable_signal: test_hard_halt_kills_inflight_at_cap records lane kills at the cap; test_under_budget_no_halt keeps DRAINING
success_criteria.text: With the hard-halt toggle armed, reaching the cap kills the in-flight lanes (DL-3) instead of draining; a run far under budget never triggers the HALT path (the gate does not over-fire).

P30-I12-W04.title: DL-4 budget HALT teeth with graceful-drain and hard-halt toggle

P30-I12-W05.description: Define a closed RiskTier StrEnum {mech, med, high, ui} plus a pure classifier assigning a wave its tier from its gate kinds (deterministic-only->mech, auditor->med, jury/UI-band->high/ui) - the mech/med/high/ui tiers do NOT exist today (distinct from OracleTier T1-T7). Gate auto-close on it: mech self-closes on deterministic checks, med on an auditor verdict, high/ui fork until I09-W04 jury_block_authority is earned.
P30-I12-W05.outcome: RiskTier {mech,med,high,ui} classifier + auto-close/fork gate; high/ui fork until block authority earned

success_criteria.measurable_signal: test_risk_tier_classifier maps gate kinds to mech/med/high/ui; test_mech_auto_closes and test_med_requires_auditor assert the close path; lane.tier set
success_criteria.text: The classifier assigns a deterministic-only wave mech (auto-closes on a deterministic pass with no human), an auditor-gated wave med (auto-closes only on a passing auditor verdict), and a jury/UI-band wave high/ui; the resolved RiskTier is recorded on the lane for the cockpit badge.

success_criteria.measurable_signal: test_high_tier_forks_until_authority asserts high/ui routes to fork while jury_block_authority is False; test_high_tier_closes_with_authority closes once granted
success_criteria.text: A high or ui RiskTier wave NEVER silently auto-closes while I09-W04 jury_block_authority is unearned: it always raises a fork; once jury_block_authority grants blocking, a high-tier wave auto-closes via the jury path. This negative path is the load-bearing safety invariant of the loop.

success_criteria.measurable_signal: test_risk_tier_enum_closed asserts the four members and that RiskTier is not OracleTier; test_classifier_pure has no state mutation
success_criteria.text: RiskTier is a closed StrEnum {mech, med, high, ui} (extra-free) distinct from OracleTier; the classifier is a pure function of the wave's gate kinds with no side effects.

P30-I12-W05.title: DL-5 define RiskTier and gate auto-close mech med auto high ui fork

P30-I12-W06.description: On a high-risk close, an uncalibrated-jury advisory, or a needs_user split, pause ONLY that lane to a fork state and enqueue a typed FleetFork; the other lanes keep draining. Resolve via approve-close / re-dispatch / skip(leave PENDING) / abort-run. This is the operator-as-decider seam FA5 renders.

success_criteria.measurable_signal: test_fork_is_lane_only asserts the forked lane state is fork, the other lanes stay running, and len(forks)==1
success_criteria.text: A fork pauses exactly its own lane to the fork state and appends one FleetFork carrying the wave, RiskTier, reason, and evidence ref; the sibling lanes remain DRAINING and keep claiming.

success_criteria.measurable_signal: test_fork_resolutions cover approve/redispatch/skip/abort outcomes; test_fork_unknown_verb_raises raises ValueError
success_criteria.text: approve-close resolves the fork to CLOSED, re-dispatch re-queues the wave, skip leaves it PENDING and frees the lane, abort halts the whole run; an unknown resolution verb raises rather than silently dropping.

P30-I12-W06.title: DL-6 lane-only blocking-fork raise and FleetFork inbox queue

P30-I12-W07.description: Extend the I06-W07 grounded repair: when the repair-attempt budget is spent the loop escalates the wave to a FleetFork tagged 'repair exhausted - your call' rather than silently dropping or looping. Closes the failure path FA6 renders.
P30-I12-W07.outcome: Repair-exhaustion escalates to FleetFork (no silent drop/re-pend)

success_criteria.measurable_signal: test_repair_exhausted_forks asserts a FleetFork with reason~=repair exhausted and the failing-check attached
success_criteria.text: A wave that fails its repair budget (e.g. 2/2 attempts spent) raises a FleetFork whose reason names repair exhaustion and carries the last failing-check payload.

success_criteria.measurable_signal: test_repair_exhausted_never_drops asserts len(forks) increments and the lane is fork, never PENDING/removed, on exhaustion
success_criteria.text: On repair exhaustion the loop NEVER leaves the lane in any state other than fork: no code path transitions an exhausted lane to PENDING or removes it without enqueuing a FleetFork (the load-bearing never-drop invariant).

P30-I12-W07.title: DL-7 escalate exhausted grounded-repair to a fork not a drop

P30-I12-W08.description: Make the FleetRun daemon-owned so it survives a TUI close and a daemon restart: on reconnect the loop reattaches to in-flight lanes via the pid registry; a lane whose session died during the blip is marked reattaching then resolved. This is the V8 session-resume the S12 scenario depends on.
P30-I12-W08.outcome: Daemon-owned fleet.reattach recovers run + re-binds live pgids; dead lanes resolved

success_criteria.measurable_signal: test_reattach_recovers_run asserts run_state and lanes restored from the persisted FleetRun and live pgids re-bound
success_criteria.text: After a simulated daemon restart mid-run, fleet.reattach recovers the persisted FleetRun and re-binds each live pgid to its lane so the run continues without re-claiming closed waves.

success_criteria.measurable_signal: test_reattach_dead_lane marks the lane reattaching then resolves it; no lane stays running with a dead pgid
success_criteria.text: A lane whose child died during the blip is set to a reattaching state then resolved (re-dispatched or marked failed), never left dangling as falsely running.

P30-I12-W08.title: DL-8 daemon-owned run resume and reattach after a TUI bounce

P30-I12-W09.description: Prove the drive loop spawns all three runtimes via the runtime-agnostic agent.dispatch path and that each lane's deny is honoured by the mechanism that runtime actually offers - this is the in-LOOP parity PROOF consuming the adapter-level deny owned by I06-W08 (codex argv) + I10-W05 (opencode), not a second implementation.
P30-I12-W09.outcome: In-loop 3-runtime cross-vendor deny parity proof via agent.dispatch

success_criteria.measurable_signal: test_drive_spawns_all_three asserts three lanes with served_runtime in {claude,codex,opencode}
success_criteria.text: A drive loop seeded with a claude, a codex, and an opencode wave spawns each through agent.dispatch(spawn=True) and records one lane per runtime with the served runtime stamped, proving the loop is runtime-agnostic.

success_criteria.measurable_signal: test_drive_deny_claude_codex asserts denied tool absent from the inverted-allowlist argv; test_drive_deny_opencode_fs_jail asserts the opencode child argv is jail-wrapped
success_criteria.text: Deny is enforced by the real per-runtime mechanism: claude/codex assert the denied tool is absent from the inverted-allowlist argv; opencode (which has no per-call deny flag) asserts the child argv is FS-jail-wrapped so writes are confined - a deny silently passing through is the failure this gate blocks.

P30-I12-W09.title: DL-9 in-loop cross-vendor deny parity per real mechanism

P30-I12-W10.description: Persist the FA7 run-summary data on FleetRun: counters {closed, failed, blocked, forksResolved}, the budget totals, throughput (wv/hr), and the terminal_reason (drained|converged|budget). The cockpit reads these; the loop never recomputes them in the UI.

success_criteria.measurable_signal: test_run_counters_persist asserts counters/totals on DONE and throughput==closed/elapsed_hours via pytest.approx; test_terminal_reason maps the three endings
success_criteria.text: On run end FleetRun carries the final counters, EU/$ totals, and throughput computed daemon-side as closed-count / elapsed-hours; the terminal_reason is exactly drained, converged, or budget matching how the run ended.

success_criteria.measurable_signal: test_terminal_reason_enum_closed asserts the three members; test_terminal_reason_none_until_done holds None mid-run

P30-I12-W11.description: The auto-drain loop spawns agents unattended, but the agent-cli failure taxonomy (RETRY_SAME -> SWITCH -> HALT with a max-total-attempts cap, RUNTIME_SPAWN_ERROR ENOENT/perm hardening, subprocess-OOM handling, and a tiered operator notice) is unwired: a runaway or repeatedly-erroring lane has no stop beyond budget. Add the bounded retry ladder + spawn-error/OOM hard-stops + a failure-toast wire so the loop is safe.
P30-I12-W11.outcome: Drive-loop failure bounds: retry cap->fork + spawn-error/OOM clean stops (I12 complete)

success_criteria.measurable_signal: test_drive_loop_failure_bounds asserts an always-fail lane stops at max_total_attempts and lands as a fork, with attempt count == the cap, not growing unbounded
success_criteria.text: A lane that keeps failing is retried at most max_total_attempts (RETRY_SAME then SWITCH), then HALTed to a fork rather than respawned forever; a test drives a always-fail lane and asserts the attempt count caps and the lane terminates, never an unbounded respawn.

success_criteria.measurable_signal: test_drive_loop_failure_bounds injects ENOENT and an OOM exit and asserts each lane ends with the typed failure reason + a failure toast while sibling lanes continue
success_criteria.text: A RUNTIME_SPAWN_ERROR (ENOENT/permission) and a subprocess-OOM each terminate the lane cleanly with a typed reason and a failure-class toast, never a silent hang or a crashed loop; other lanes keep draining.

P30-I12-W11.title: DL-11 bound the drive-loop with retry caps and OOM/spawn-error stops
